title: Responsive cost tiles — microstates, motion specs, and edge-case polish
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Finalize visual and interaction specs for the new responsive cost tiles used across the Redwood Console cost overview and per-route dashboards. This ticket focuses on microstates (hover, focus, loading, empty, error), motion timing for token/usage updates, and explicit edge-case designs for narrow widths and high-card counts. Goal is a dev-ready redline set + prototype and a short QA checklist for the first implementation iteration.

Context: The cost tiles are used on the global cost dashboard and per-route cost pages. We recently changed the data model to support live incremental updates (streaming delta for token counts) and need the UI to reflect incremental vs final updates without visual jitter. Engineering is implementing the runtime-driven streaming updates and needs clear guidance on staged content replacement, skeletons vs micro-animations, and accessibility semantics for dynamic content updates.

This ticket covers:
- Motion specs for incremental token updates vs full tile refresh.
- Loading/skeleton states and how to transition to populated states.
- Compact tile layout for <480px widths and grid reflow rules.
- Error and empty states with recovery CTAs.
- Microcopy for tooltips and ARIA-live message content.
- Redline assets and a Figma prototype link for dev handoff.

Prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/Example/Redwood-Cost-Tiles-Proto (dedicated frame: Responsive-Cost-Tiles-v3)
Implementation notes: The streaming update badge should appear for short lived updates (<5s) and fade using a 220ms ease-out. For large deltas (>20% change) we use a subtle pulse to call attention rather than a persistent badge.
acceptance_criteria: Figma redlines published in the 'Responsive-Cost-Tiles-v3' frame
Prototype demonstrates hover/focus/loading/error/empty states across 320/480/720/1200 widths
Motion tokens (duration/easing/opacity transforms) documented and annotated on each component
Accessibility notes: ARIA-live region content samples provided for streaming vs final update
Dev has a single merged artifact (figma + CSS guidance + sample JSON payloads) to implement
decisions: Use a 220ms ease-out for small token count fades and 360ms spring-like pulse for large delta highlights
Prefer skeleton shimmer for initial tile load, but use inline shimmer -> static content transition for streaming updates to prevent layout shift
Badge for 'live update' shown only when data is partial; badge text: 'Updating' with accessible label 'Cost tile is updating in real time'
Compact layout collapses the secondary meta row into an overflow menu at widths <360px instead of truncating important metrics
open_issues: Need final wording for failure CTA when the per-route cost API returns partial data (PM feedback pending)
Edge-case: how to handle >50 tiles rendering on a single page — potential virtualization requirement (engineering to advise)
Coordination with Analytics team for click tracking on the 'details' chevron to ensure instrumentation names
comments: 2026-03-02 - Marco Reyes (Design): Uploaded first redlines. Noting that engineering prefers CSS-only transitions where possible. Asked for a fallback plan for older browsers.

2026-03-04 - Priya Shah (Product): PM note — prioritize the mobile compact tile for the upcoming demo. We can defer the >50 tiles performance work to a follow-up but need acceptance criteria for demo devices.

2026-03-05 - Evan Liu (Frontend Eng): Reviewed motion specs. Suggest we reduce pulse amplitude on large deltas to avoid perceived 'flashing'. Also: will need example JSON showing streaming partial/complete payload shapes.

2026-03-06 - Accessibility review (Lina Gomez): ARIA-live guidance looks good; recommend adding 'role=status' on the updated value and ensure color-only states are accompanied by icons/text for colorblind users.
2026-03-08 - Marco Reyes: Updated prototype with revised microcopy ('Updating' -> 'Live update') and added aria examples. Left a note that this was a product/PM suggestion.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Design Lead): Minor redlines applied: increased hit target on tile CTA to 44px, clarified contrast for delta percent text. Please review before handing off to ENG.

2026-03-11 - QA (Jordan Kim): Will run cross-device checks against acceptance criteria after dev build. Flagged potential issue: skeleton shimmer timing looks off on slow devices; might need a reduced frame-rate friendly approach.
qa_checklist: Verify skeleton -> content transition on 3G/Slow 4G throttling in Chrome DevTools
Confirm ARIA-live announcements use non-verbose copy and don't duplicate when multiple tiles update simultaneously
Check focus states via keyboard navigation for each tile interactive element
Validate visual delta treatments for small (<=20%) vs large (>20%) token changes
Confirm compact breakpoint layout at 320px and 360px with both LTR and RTL locales
